gloss: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-23: 'water' IS attested in DB (ARIo Q007134): "aniya apiyā āhyatā apišim parābara" (others were thrown into the water, the water carried them off) — see api-. The earlier scan looked for ap-/āp- forms in another normalisation and missed them (research/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md Q-130).
source: ORACC ARIo (Schmitt 2009 ed., digitized by H. Heitmann-Gordon, MOCCI; CC0) via GitHub mirror SLAB-NLP/Akk data/jsonl/ario.jsonl

gloss: water (loc. apiyā 'into the water'; apišim 'the water [carried] them')
attested: DB (ARIo Q007134): "aniya apiyā āhyatā apišim parābara" (others were thrown into the water, the water carried them off)
source: form: ORACC ARIo (Schmitt 2009 ed., digitized by H. Heitmann-Gordon, MOCCI; CC0) via GitHub mirror SLAB-NLP/Akk data/jsonl/ario.jsonl; gloss: from context in the ARIo text (no translation of this passage read in this pass; standard meaning, Kent 1953 NOT SEEN)
note: Attested in DB, so the earlier '(water)' absence entry was wrong (logged Q-130). ARIo spells apiyā with short a (Kent āpiyā). Only the locative is attested; a bare 'water!' (nom. *āpiš) is not. Kent-style spelling: âpiyâ.

gloss: day (DB date formula 'Garmapadahya māhyā 1 rau̯ca θakatam āha': one day of Garmapada had passed; pl. rau̯cabiš)
attested: DB (ARIo Q007134): "Garmapadahya māhyā 1 rau̯ca θakatam"; rau̯cabiš 18× in date formulas
source: form: ORACC ARIo (Schmitt 2009 ed., digitized by H. Heitmann-Gordon, MOCCI; CC0) via GitHub mirror SLAB-NLP/Akk data/jsonl/ario.jsonl; gloss: from context in the ARIo text (no translation of this passage read in this pass; standard meaning, Kent 1953 NOT SEEN)
note: The meaning follows from the formula month + numeral + rau̯ca(biš) + θakatā "had passed". Kent-style spelling: rauca.

source: form: ORACC ARIo (Schmitt 2009 ed., digitized by H. Heitmann-Gordon, MOCCI; CC0) via GitHub mirror SLAB-NLP/Akk data/jsonl/ario.jsonl; gloss: Livius.org translation (scraped copy in Electronic-Old-Persian-Library/Old-Persian-Dataset textdata/web_scraping/)
